Workers and companies in all sectors can contribute their skills to meet society new needs.

We keeps a horse, two cows, and six chickens.
questions.solution: B) The sentence should be corrected as "We keep a horse, two cows, and six chickens." The reason is that the pronoun "we" takes a plural verb form, "keep" in this case

Q10. Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.
P. undermining the strict application of comparative anthropology
Q. in the early 20th century it was almost universally assumed

Q13. Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose ‘No improvement’ as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.
If proper treat, the wound should heal within a few weeks.
questions.solution:
B) Properly treated
"treat" is a verb and needs an adverb (in this case "properly") to modify it, and it also needs to be in the passive voice ("treated") to fit with the structure of the sentence. Hence, "properly treated" is the correct choice.

Q14. Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose
‘No error’.
We have more then 6 years of experience in field hockey.
questions.solution: A) "then" should be replaced with "than" because "Than" is used in comparisons, while "then" is used to denote time or sequence. in this sentence, where a comparison is being made between the amount of experience "we" have and a duration of six years.

Q16. Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement’.
But what of the young people whom are part of the cricket crowds, some of who are presumably born in England?
options: who are part of the cricket crowds, some of who are presumably born in England
whom are part of the cricket crowds, some of whom are presumably born in England
who are part of the cricket crowds, some of whom are presumably born in England
questions.solution: D) "who" is correctly used as the subject in the phrase "who are part of the cricket crowds", but "whom" should be used as the object of the preposition "of" in the phrase "some of whom are presumably born in England". Thus, option D is the grammatically correct improvement to the sentence.

questions.q:
Q18. Given below are four jumbled sentences. Pick the option that gives their correct order.
P. In July 1977, Marley was found to have a type of malignant melanoma (cancer) under the nail of a toe.
Q. He died on 11 May 1981 at Cedars of Lebanon Hospital in Miami (now University of Miami Hospital) at the age of 36.
R. Despite his illness, he continued touring until his health deteriorated as the cancer had spread throughout his body.
S. Marley turned down his doctors' advice to have his toe amputated, citing his religious beliefs.
questions.solution:
A)PSRQ
In July 1977, Marley was found to have a type of malignant melanoma (cancer) under the nail of a toe. Marley turned down his doctors' advice to have his toe amputated, citing his religious beliefs. Despite his illness, he continued touring until his health deteriorated as the cancer had spread throughout his body. He died on 11 May 1981 at Cedars of Lebanon Hospital in Miami (now University of Miami Hospital) at the age of 36.

questions.q:
Comprehension:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.
Yes, there’s definitely something to be said about (1) ______ the perfect cup of coffee. I’m staring (2) ______ the machine again, but today I’m smiling. I’ve done it – the correct amount of foam, the (3) ______ like silk and the little dusting of chocolate, (4) ______ a perfect heart on the top. It’s just a shame that it’s me who is drinking it, not a/an (5) ______ customer.
Q21. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.solution:
B)Making
The sentence will read as: "Yes, there’s definitely something to be said about making the perfect cup of coffee." This makes the most sense given the context of the passage, as the speaker is discussing the process of creating an ideal cup of coffee. The options 'sobbing', 'breaking', and 'loading' do not fit contextually with the act of preparing a cup of coffee.
